entities.summary: The Institute for Palestine Studies (IPS) is the oldest independent nonprofit public service research institute in the Arab world. It was established and incorporated in Beirut, Lebanon, in 1963 and has since served as a model for other such institutes in the region. It is the only institute solely concerned with analyzing and documenting Palestinian affairs and the Arab–Israeli conflict. It also publishes scholarly journals and has published more than 600 books, monographs, and documentary collections in English, Arabic and French—as well as its quarterly academic journals: Journal of Palestine Studies, Jerusalem Quarterly, and Majallat al-Dirasat al-Filistiniyyah.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Institute for Palestine Studies has played a crucial role in documenting and analyzing Palestinian affairs and the Arab–Israeli conflict since its establishment in 1963. Its publications have provided valuable insights into the region's complex history and politics.
